rationales: Carbon (spelled “Carban” here) is abundant in protoplasm but not the most abundant element.
Hydrogen is present in protoplasm but in a lower percentage than oxygen.
Oxygen makes up the highest percentage of protoplasm.
Nitrogen is present in a lower percentage than oxygen.
A population is a group of individuals of the same species in an area.
The biosphere is the part of Earth inhabited by organisms and their communities.
A species is a group of similar organisms, not the inhabited part of Earth.
Coordination means the harmonious working of body parts, not an inhabited region.
A hypothesis is proposed after observations have been made.
Deduction is reasoning from a hypothesis to a prediction.
Experiments test a hypothesis and are not the basic first step.
Observation is the basic starting step of the biological method.
Allium cepa is the scientific name of onion.
“Zia-maize” is not the scientific name of starfish.
Asterias rubens is a scientific name for a sea star.
Corvus splendens is the scientific name of the house crow.
Chitin is found in fungal cell walls and the exoskeletons of arthropods.
Lignin strengthens some plant cell walls but is not their main basic component.
Cellulose is the main structural material in plant cell walls.
Plasmodesmata are channels between plant cells, not cell-wall material.
Germ cells give rise to gametes and do not form most of the body.
Gametes are reproductive cells, not the cells that form the body.
Somatic cells form the body of an organism.
Parent cells divide to produce daughter cells and are not the general name for body cells.
Lipase breaks down fats.
Protease breaks down proteins.
Amylase breaks down starch.
Pepsin digests proteins in the stomach.
Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm.
The nucleus is not the site of glycolysis.
Mitochondria carry out later stages of cellular respiration, not glycolysis.
Chloroplasts are not the site of glycolysis.
Pepsinogen is activated to form pepsin in the stomach.
Bicarbonate does not result from the activation of pepsinogen.
Hydrochloric acid helps activate pepsinogen but is not its product.
Gastrin is a hormone that regulates gastric activity, not the product of pepsinogen activation.
Glucose is commonly converted into sucrose for transport in most plants.
Sucrose is the main form in which food is transported through most plants.
Starch is generally stored rather than transported through plants.
Protein is not the usual transported form of food in plants.
The left atrium has thinner walls than the ventricles.
The right atrium has thinner walls than the ventricles.
The left ventricle has the thickest wall because it pumps blood throughout the body.
The right ventricle pumps blood only to the lungs and has a thinner wall than the left ventricle.
Biology is the study of life in general.
Zoology is the scientific study of animals.
Botany is the scientific study of plants.
Microbiology is the study of microorganisms.
Jabir Bin Hayan was a prominent early scholar, but not the author of this book.
Abdul Malik Asmai was a scholar of natural history, not the author of this medical text.
Bu Ali Sina (Avicenna) wrote Al-Qanun-fil-Tib.
Robert Brown was a botanist known for describing the cell nucleus.
A theory is a well-supported explanation that has withstood repeated testing.
A law describes a consistent pattern or relationship, rather than an un-rejected hypothesis.
A principle is a general foundational rule or concept, not the term defined here.
A deduction is a conclusion derived from a hypothesis or other information.
The family name is not the first word of a binomial scientific name.
The class name is not part of the two-word binomial name.
The genus name comes first and its first letter is capitalized.
The species name comes second and is written in lowercase.
